newsitem.title: USA: Supervalu still seeks to exist ShopKo holding.
newsitem.headline: Supervalu still seeks to exist ShopKo holding.

text.p: Supervalu Inc said Wednesday it remains comitted to exiting its investment in Shopko Stores Inc, but supports the decision by ShopKo and Phar-Mor Inc to end their planned business combination.
Supervalu acquired ShopKo in 1971 and then sold 54 percent of that company's stock in a 1991 public offering.
Earlier, ShopKo and Phar-Mor said they terminated by mutual agreement their planned business combination that was first announced in September 1996.
The companies said in a statement that due to continuing uncertainties in consummating the transaction they will pursue their respective goals separately.

"Supervalu supports the companies' decision to end the agreement," Mike Wright, chairman, said in a statement. "We are pleased that ShopKo has continued its strong financial performance during the last six months despite the uncertainty created by the proposed transaction."

Under the proposed transaction that was terminated, Cabot Noble Inc, the holding company formed for the proposed transaction, would have repurchased approximately 90 percent of Supervalu's 14.7 million shares of ShopKo for about $223.6 million. Supervalu would have retained $25 million in Cabot Noble stock that it would have received in the transaction.
